mainTopic: How מליקה is done, and when a creature counts as dead for טומאה even while it still moves
overview: The גמרא first solves a difficulty in זעירי's statement about מליקה. רבא, and רבי אמי in a story with רבי זירא, explain that the כהן cuts the spine and neck bone without most of the flesh, so the bird is still alive. A ברייתא supports this. The גמרא then asks whether its rule of 'two or most of two' סימנים for an עולה follows the רבנן or רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and gives two answers. Next come rulings on when an injured creature already counts as dead even though it still moves. For a person, this is a broken מפרקת with most of the flesh, or being torn open like a fish from the back; עלי's death is explained by his old age. For an animal, it is being cut in half across its width, or losing a thigh so that the gap shows even while it lies down. The גמרא then discusses the משנה about creatures whose heads were הותזו: ריש לקיש says fully cut off, and רבי אסי says cut like a bird עולה according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Finally it begins quoting the ברייתא behind that argument, which compares the bird עולה to an animal חטאת, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The difficulty with זעירי's statement remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that, whatever was said before, זעירי's statement is still difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that זעירי's statement is still a problem. This line sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי spoke about breaking the spine and neck bone together with most of the flesh during מליקה. Once that much is cut, the bird is considered dead. So why would anyone keep doing מליקה on a dead bird?

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; whatever we said before
It is difficult; an unresolved problem

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: This goes back to זעירי's statement from before. Read plainly, it sounds like the bird is already dead before the מליקה is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the open difficulty on זעירי's statement after a side discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's statement about breaking the spine and neck bone together with most of the flesh in מליקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If most of the flesh is cut along with the spine, the bird is already dead, and there is no point in continuing the מליקה on a dead bird.

steps.title: רבא rereads the statement: without most of the flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the כהן cuts the spine and neck bone without cutting most of the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Read it this way: 'And this is how he does it: he cuts the spine and the neck bone without most of the flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the difficulty by changing how we read זעירי's words. The כהן cuts the spine and neck bone but leaves most of the flesh uncut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most of the flesh is not cut, the bird is still alive when the כהן reaches the סימנים. Now the מליקה makes sense, because it is done on a living bird. The statement is no longer a ruling about a dead bird. It is a description of the right way to do מליקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read it this way (used to reread a statement)
Spinal column
Neck bone
Most of the surrounding flesh

phrases.english: Rava said: Say:
And this is how he does it –
he cuts the spine and the neck bone
without most of the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement describes cutting most of the flesh, which would kill the bird before the מליקה is done.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement describes how מליקה is done: the spine and neck bone are cut without most of the flesh, so the bird stays alive.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא came to ארץ ישראל, he heard רבי אמי teaching זעירי's statement and asked how one can do מליקה on a dead bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי אמי sitting and teaching this ruling. He said to him: Does a person stand and do מליקה on a dead bird?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which the same difficulty is raised again. רבי זירא challenges רבי אמי, who was teaching זעירי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same problem as in step 1, now told as a real conversation. רבי זירא understood the statement to mean most of the flesh is cut. If so, the bird is already dead, and continuing the מליקה would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
A teaching or ruling
A dead bird
Does מליקה (pinches the neck of a bird offering)

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: He moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Ami sitting
and teaching this ruling.
phrases.notes: This is זעירי's statement that the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מֵתָה עוֹמֵד וּמוֹלֵק?
phrases.english: He said to him: Does one stand and do melikah on a dead bird?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story in which the difficulty from step 1 is raised again.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's statement as taught by רבי אמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting most of the flesh kills the bird, so it makes no sense to keep doing מליקה on it.

steps.title: רבי אמי gives the same answer as רבא
steps.stepSummary: After a moment of surprise, רבי אמי answers that the spine and neck bone are cut without most of the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was stunned for a moment. Then he said to him: Read it this way: this is how he does it: he cuts the spine and the neck bone without most of the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי is caught off guard at first. Then he gives the same answer רבא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate אמוראים reach the same reading, which makes it stronger. The bird stays alive because most of the flesh is not cut, so the מליקה is done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Was stunned or astonished
For a moment

phrases.english: He was stunned for a moment,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אמי. The same words appear in דניאל 4:16.

phrases.english: he said to him: Say,
this is how he does it:
he cuts the spine and the neck bone
without most of the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge with the same reading רבא gave.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Most of the flesh is cut, so the bird is dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most of the flesh is not cut, so the bird is alive during the מליקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this method of מליקה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes מליקה just this way, and adds how many סימנים are cut for a חטאת העוף and for an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: How is מליקה done on a חטאת העוף? He cuts the spine and neck bone without most of the flesh until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe. Once he reaches the gullet or the windpipe, he cuts one סימן or most of it, together with most of the flesh. For an עולה, he cuts two סימנים or most of two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבא's and רבי אמי's answer. It also adds details about cutting the סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says clearly that the spine and neck bone are cut 'without most of the flesh', which is exactly the reading given above. It then gives a new rule: a חטאת העוף needs one סימן or most of one. An עולה needs two סימנים or most of two.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a sin offering
The gullet (food pipe)
The windpipe
One of the two organs (gullet or windpipe) cut in שחיטה or מליקה
A burnt offering

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא confirms the rereading of זעירי. Its rule about 'two or most of two' for an עולה leads straight into the next question.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
How does one do melikah on a bird sin offering?
He cuts the spine and the neck bone
without most of the flesh
until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe;
once he has reached the gullet or the windpipe,
he cuts one siman or most of it
and most of the flesh with it,
and for a burnt offering, two or most of two.
phrases.notes: He means two סימנים, or most of each of the two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in steps 2 and 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the spine and neck bone are cut without most of the flesh
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing how מליקה is done on a חטאת העוף

steps.title: Which תנא does the ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows, since the רבנן require exactly two סימנים and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires most of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is the רבנן, they say exactly two! If it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, he says most of two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the ברייתא. Neither known opinion seems to fit its rule for an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows either 'two or most of two' for an עולה. The רבנן require exactly two whole סימנים, so they would not allow 'most of two'. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says most of two, so why would the ברייתא mention cutting two? The ברייתא's mix of both options does not match either opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Which תנא is the author?
Specifically; exactly this and nothing else
Most of each of the two סימנים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is being rejected. The גמרא only wants to know which תנא it fits, because its 'two or most of two' wording seems to fall between the two known opinions.

phrases.english: Who is it? If it is the Rabbis –
don't they say: specifically two!
If it follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon –
doesn't he say: most of two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who wrote the ברייתא that was just brought as support.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that an עולה needs 'two or most of two' סימנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן require exactly two, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires most of two. Neither one matches a ruling that allows both options.

steps.title: Split the ברייתא Between Two Opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'two' in the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and 'most of two' follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say this: where the ברייתא says 'two,' it follows the רבנן. Where it says 'most of two,' it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. It says the ברייתא does not follow just one opinion. Each part follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that 'two' and 'most of two' cannot both fit one opinion. This answer avoids the problem by giving 'two' to the רבנן and 'most of two' to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Under this answer, the ברייתא is a mix of two views.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the source this way)
Two (both סימנים fully cut)
Most of each of the two סימנים

phrases.english: Say: 'two' is according to the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 5, about how many סימנים are cut for a חטאת העוף and an עולה.

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב שְׁנַיִם – לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: 'most of two' is according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 about whose view the ברייתא follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: different parts follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow one opinion, and neither fits both phrases.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Two' follows the רבנן, and 'most of two' follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: Second Answer: All of It Follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the whole ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and 'two' means a cut so large that it looks like two whole סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say that both parts follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. What does 'two' mean? A cut that looks like two full סימנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. The whole ברייתא follows one opinion, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'two' does not mean two complete סימנים. It means cutting so much of them that it looks almost like two full ones. So 'two' and 'most of two' both mean a large majority, and the ברייתא stays with one opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternative answer)
Both this and that
That look like two (a very large majority)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'two' here means the רבנן's view of two complete סימנים. In this answer 'two' is just a way of describing a very large majority cut.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: both this and that are Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
and what does 'two' mean? That which looks like two.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same question, without splitting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word: 'two' means a cut that looks like two, not two complete סימנים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Two' means two complete סימנים, which only the רבנן hold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון; 'two' means a near-complete majority.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the ברייתא: split it between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, or read all of it as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון with 'two' meaning 'like two.'

steps.title: Broken Neck Bone With Most of the Flesh
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a person's מפרקת is broken along with most of the flesh around it, he makes things impure in a tent like a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if the מפרקת is broken and most of the flesh with it, the person makes things impure in a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a person. It explains when a broken neck already makes him count as dead for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the person is still moving, a broken מפרקת together with most of the surrounding flesh gives him the status of a dead body. So anyone under the same roof becomes טמא. This connects to the earlier steps, which also spoke about cutting the מפרקת with or without most of the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Neck bone / spine at the neck
Most of the flesh
Makes impure in a tent (anyone under the same roof), like a dead body

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the point at which an injured person is treated as dead for טומאת מת, even before he stops moving.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If the neck bone was broken
and most of the flesh with it,
he makes things impure in a tent.
phrases.notes: He counts as a dead body, even if he is still moving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מליקה of a bird to the same kind of injury in a person, for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken מפרקת together with most of the flesh gives a person the status of a dead body for טומאת אהל.

steps.title: What About עלי's Death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a challenge: עלי died from a broken מפרקת even though most of the flesh was not cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: in that story of עלי, it was only the מפרקת, without most of the flesh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge to שמואל's rule from the story of עלי the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needs both the מפרקת and most of the flesh. But עלי fell, broke only his neck, and died right away. That seems to show that a broken מפרקת alone is enough to cause death.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
Incident, story
Without

phrases.english: And if you will say:
that incident of Eli,
phrases.notes: עלי the כהן גדול, who fell and broke his neck (שמואל א 4:18).

phrases.english: it was the neck bone without most of the flesh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's requirement of most of the flesh.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that most of the flesh must be broken with the מפרקת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עלי died from a broken neck alone, so the flesh should not be needed.

steps.title: Old Age Is Different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עלי was very old and heavy, so a broken neck alone was enough to kill him, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Old age is different, as it is written: 'When he mentioned the Ark of God, he fell backward off the chair by the side of the gate, his neck broke and he died, for the man was old and heavy...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. עלי's case was special because of his age, and it proves this from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself gives the reason: 'for the man was old and heavy.' So עלי died from a broken neck alone only because he was old and weak. For a normal person, שמואל's rule still needs most of the flesh too.

keyTerms.meaning: Old age
Is different
As it is written
The Ark of God

phrases.english: Old age is different,
as it is written:
'And it was when he mentioned the Ark of God,'
'he fell off the chair backward'
'by the side of the gate,'
'and his neck broke and he died,'
'for the man was old and heavy, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from עלי by showing his case was an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is an exception, using the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עלי's death shows that a broken neck alone makes a person count as dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: עלי was old and heavy, so his case is special; שמואל's rule for a normal person stands.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a broken מפרקת with most of the flesh means the person counts as dead. עלי died from the neck alone only because he was old and heavy.

steps.title: Torn Open Like a Fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a person torn open the long way, like a fish, makes things impure in a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone tore him open like a fish, he makes things impure in a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where an injured person already counts as dead for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person torn open the long way, the way a fish is cut, is treated as a dead body even if he is still moving. So he makes things impure in a tent, just like the broken-neck case.

keyTerms.meaning: He tore him open
Like a fish (cut the long way)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one tore him open like a fish,
he makes things impure in a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case, alongside שמואל's, where an injured person counts as dead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person torn open like a fish has the status of a dead body for טומאת אהל.

steps.title: Only If Torn From the Back
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק limits רבי יוחנן's rule: it applies when the person was torn open from his back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: and from his back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר יצחק adds a limit to רבי יוחנן's ruling, saying exactly how the tearing must be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about tearing 'like a fish' applies when the tear is from the back. This narrows the case in which the person counts as dead.

keyTerms.meaning: From his back

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
And from his back.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's rule is talking about a person torn open from the back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: וּמִגַּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being torn like a fish counts as death for טומאת אהל when the tear is from the back.
steps.whatToRemember: A person torn open like a fish counts as dead for טומאת אהל, and רבי שמואל בר יצחק adds that this is when the tear is from the back.

steps.title: An animal cut in half across its width is a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that an animal cut through across its width, like a broken shard, already has the status of a נבלה, even if it is still moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If someone made the animal like a shard (cut it in two across its width), it is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from the rulings about people to rulings about animals. שמואל gives a new ruling about an animal cut in two across its width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier rulings about a person, the point is that some injuries are so final that the creature counts as dead right away, even while it still twitches. Here the injury is cutting the animal in two across its width, and the result is that it is treated as a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A broken piece of pottery, a shard. Here it describes an animal cut in two across its width.
An animal that died without proper שחיטה. It is forbidden to eat and makes things impure.
He made it into.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
If one made it (the animal) like a shard, it is a נבלה.
phrases.notes: He means the animal was cut in two across its width, like a broken piece of pottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rulings about a person (steps 9-13) to a parallel ruling about an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal cut in two across its width is a נבלה even while it still moves.

steps.title: An animal with its thigh removed is a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that if an animal's thigh was removed and the hollow where it was is visible, the animal is a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: If the thigh was removed and its hollow is visible, it is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds another injury that makes a living animal count as a נבלה: losing its hind thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only applies when the empty space left by the thigh can be seen. That condition is unclear, and the גמרא asks about it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The thigh, meaning the animal's hind leg.
A hollow or empty space. Here it is the spot where the thigh used to be.
Visible, easy to notice.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
If the thigh was removed
and its hollow is visible, it is a נבלה.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, נִיכָּר ('visible').

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נִיטַּל הַיָּרֵךְ וְחָלָל שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second injury to שמואל's list of injuries that make an animal a נבלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal whose thigh was removed, leaving a visible hollow, is a נבלה.

steps.title: When is the thigh's hollow considered visible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case is meant by the hollow of the thigh being visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'its hollow is visible'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי אלעזר's words. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any animal missing a leg has an empty spot there. So the גמרא wants to know exactly how 'visible' the hollow must be for the animal to count as a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case of its hollow being visible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a condition in רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation in which the thigh's hollow counts as visible.

steps.title: רבא: The animal is lying down and still looks like it is missing a part
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the hollow counts as visible when the animal is lying down and you can still see that it is missing a part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Any case where it is lying down and still looks like it is missing something.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The hollow counts as visible when you can see the missing part even while the animal is lying down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal lies down, its body tends to cover up small gaps. If the missing thigh can still be seen in that position, the loss is big enough to make the animal a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying down, crouched on the ground.
Missing something, lacking a part.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Any case where it is lying down and still looks like it is missing something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hollow counts as visible when the animal is lying down and can still be seen to be missing a part.

steps.title: משנה: Creatures whose heads were removed are impure even while they twitch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that says creatures whose heads were removed are impure even while they still twitch, just like a lizard's cut-off tail that twitches.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: If their heads were removed, even though they twitch, they are impure, like the tail of a lizard that twitches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from somewhere else. It does this to examine one word in it, הותזו, in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that twitching is not a sign of life. Once the head is removed, the creature counts as dead and is impure. A lizard's tail that keeps moving after it is cut off is the example: it moves, but it is not alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Were removed or chopped off. The גמרא will ask exactly what this means.
Twitching, convulsing.
A lizard.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in אהלות 1:6.

phrases.english: If their heads were removed,
even though they twitch, they are impure,
like the tail of a lizard that twitches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה on the same theme, that a creature can count as dead while it still moves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creatures whose heads were removed are impure even while they twitch.

steps.title: What does הותזו mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word הותזו in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'were removed' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by the heads being הותזו. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how much cutting is needed. Does the head have to be completely cut off, or is a smaller cut enough to make the creature count as dead?

keyTerms.meaning: What? What does it mean?

phrases.english: What is meant by 'were removed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much cutting of the head the word הותזו requires.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The head is actually cut off
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says הותזו means exactly what it says: the head is completely cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Actually removed.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the first answer. The head must be fully cut off from the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the word in its plain sense sets a strict standard. Only a head that is completely separated makes the twitching body count as dead.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, literally.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
Actually removed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הותזו means the head is completely cut off.

steps.title: רבי אסי quoting רבי מני: Like separating the head of a bird עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי, quoting רבי מני, says הותזו means the head is cut the way the head of a bird עולה is separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני: Like the separation of the bird burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to what הותזו means. The measure is taken from the way the כהן separates the head of a bird brought as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of requiring the head to be fully cut off, this answer uses a known standard from the קרבנות. That standard may be less than a complete cut-off, and the next step asks exactly how much it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Separation. Here it means separating the bird's head during the קרבן.
A bird brought as an עולה (burnt offering), whose head the כהן separates.

phrases.english: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני:
Like the separation of the bird burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי: כְּהַבְדָּלַת עוֹלַת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, different from ריש לקיש's, to the question in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הותזו means cut the way the head of a bird עולה is separated.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks: Which way of separating the bird's head do you mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אסי whether he means separating the bird's head as the רבנן describe it, so that he agrees with ריש לקיש, or as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון describes it, so that the two of them disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי אסי: Do you mean like the separation of the bird burnt offering according to the רבנן, and then you do not disagree? Or perhaps like the separation of the bird burnt offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and then you disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אסי to clarify his answer. There is more than one opinion about how a bird עולה's head is separated, and the answer decides whether he and ריש לקיש really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the bird's head is cut so thoroughly that hardly anything holds it on, which is practically the same as ריש לקיש's 'actually removed.' According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, cutting most of the two סימנים is enough. That would be less than a full cut-off, so רבי אסי and ריש לקיש would disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural) disagree.
Or perhaps.
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of הותזו: ריש לקיש says the head is fully cut off, and רבי אסי says it is cut like the head of a bird עולה. Whether they truly disagree depends on which opinion about the bird עולה רבי אסי follows.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said to רבי אסי:
Do you mean like the separation of the bird burnt offering according to the רבנן,
and then you do not disagree,
phrases.notes: 'You' means רבי אסי and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: or perhaps like the separation of the bird burnt offering
according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון,
and then you disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי אַסִּי: כְּהַבְדָּלַת עוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רבי אסי's answer in step 21 really differs from ריש לקיש's answer in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אסי follows the רבנן's measure for separating the bird's head (so he agrees with ריש לקיש) or רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's measure (so they disagree).

steps.title: רבי אסי says he follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers רבי ירמיה. He means separating the head the way רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון describes it, so he and ריש לקיש really disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Like the separation of the bird burnt offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and we disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the question from the last step. He means separating the head according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so his view really is different from ריש לקיש's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה gave two choices: the רבנן's way, which would agree with ריש לקיש, or רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's way, which would argue with him. רבי אסי picks the second choice. So in his view הותזו does not have to mean the head is cut off completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating, here meaning cutting the bird's head off from its body
A burnt offering brought from a bird
And we disagree (רבי אסי and ריש לקיש)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אסי answering רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: Like the separation of the bird burnt offering
according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
and we disagree.
phrases.notes: "We" means רבי אסי and ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּהַבְדָּלַת עוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's either-or question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He means רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's way of separating the head, so he disagrees with ריש לקיש.

steps.title: A second version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: Another version tells it directly. ריש לקיש says the head is fully cut off. רבי אסי, quoting רבי מני, says it means separating the head as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון describes it, which is cutting most of the two סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: 'Removed' literally. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני: Like the separation of the bird burnt offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, with most of the two סימנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the same argument. In this version there is no back-and-forth with רבי ירמיה; רבי אסי's opinion is stated plainly from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version we needed רבי ירמיה's question to learn which view רבי אסי meant. Here רבי אסי says directly: like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, cutting most of the two סימנים. Both versions end the same way, with ריש לקיש and רבי אסי disagreeing.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually or literally, meaning completely cut off
Most of the two סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument or a new opinion. It is the same argument told in a different way, without רבי ירמיה's question.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
"Removed" literally,
Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Mani:
Like the separation of the bird burnt offering
according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
with most of the two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the same argument again, in a different version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש: completely cut off. רבי אסי quoting רבי מני: most of the two סימנים, like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way. For ריש לקיש, הותזו means the head is completely off. For רבי אסי, cutting most of the two סימנים, as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון describes it, is enough.

steps.title: What do the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון each hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the argument between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about the bird עולה comes from, and what each side says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of the רבנן, and what is the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the background argument it has been relying on. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole explanation of הותזו depends on how the bird עולה's head is separated. So the גמרא now wants the actual source that shows each side's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view in the argument

phrases.english: What is the view of the Rabbis
and what is the view of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבָּנַן וּמַאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the argument that the last steps mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and details of the argument between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about separating the bird עולה's head.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins with the words "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט"
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts with a ברייתא on the poor person's offering. The second bird is made an עולה "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט", and that means like the rule of an animal חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: "And the second he shall make a burnt offering according to the rule" means according to the rule of an animal sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the word "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" in the פסוק about the second bird, which is brought as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person brings two birds instead of an animal: one as a חטאת and one as an עולה. The ברייתא says "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" ties the bird עולה to the rules of an animal חטאת. This reading will lead to the argument about separating the head.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
According to the rule or set procedure
A sin offering brought from an animal

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"And the second he shall make a burnt offering
according to the rule"
means according to the rule of an animal sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְאֶת הַשֵּׁנִי יַעֲשֶׂה עֹלָה כַּמִּשְׁפָּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא that reads "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" as "like the rule of an animal חטאת".

steps.title: Maybe it means like a bird חטאת instead?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, someone asks: why read "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" as the rule of an animal חטאת? Maybe it means the rule of a bird חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means according to the rule of an animal sin offering. Or perhaps it means only according to the rule of a bird sin offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. It suggests the second bird might follow the rules of the first bird, the bird חטאת, instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing a bird to a bird seems more natural, since the two birds are brought together. So the ברייתא must show why the comparison is to an animal חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: You say... or perhaps it is only..., a ברייתא's way of raising another possible reading
A sin offering brought from a bird

phrases.english: You say according to the rule of an animal sin offering,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּמִשְׁפַּט חַטַּאת הָעוֹף?
phrases.english: or perhaps it means only according to the rule of a bird sin offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כְּמִשְׁפַּט חַטַּאת בְּהֵמָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּמִשְׁפַּט חַטַּאת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading the ברייתא just gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" points to an animal חטאת and not a bird חטאת.

steps.title: "וְהִקְרִיבוֹ" shows the bird עולה is different from the bird חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The word "וְהִקְרִיבוֹ" shows the תורה set the bird עולה apart from the bird חטאת. So "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" must mean like an animal חטאת. The ברייתא then starts comparing the two, and the comparison continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says "and he shall bring it", the פסוק separated a bird sin offering from a bird burnt offering. So how do I explain "according to the rule"? According to the rule of an animal sin offering. Just as an animal sin offering comes only...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. A different פסוק already shows that a bird עולה is not done like a bird חטאת, so "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" must mean like an animal חטאת. The ברייתא then starts a comparison that continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since "וְהִקְרִיבוֹ" already tells us the bird עולה is not like the bird חטאת, the bird חטאת cannot be what "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" refers to. The only choice left is an animal חטאת. The words "מָה חַטַּאת בְּהֵמָה" begin a "just as... so too..." comparison, which will show what the bird עולה learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bring it, the פסוק about a bird עולה
The פסוק made a distinction
How do I explain or apply this word

phrases.english: When it says "and he shall bring it,"
the verse made a distinction
between a bird sin offering and a bird burnt offering,
so how do I explain "according to the rule"?
According to the rule of an animal sin offering.
Just as an animal sin offering comes only...

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר וְהִקְרִיבוֹ, חִלֵּק הַכָּתוּב בֵּין חַטַּאת הָעוֹף לְעוֹלַת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "וְהִקְרִיבוֹ" separates the bird עולה from the bird חטאת, so "כַּמִּשְׁפָּט" must mean like an animal חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: Comparing the bird עולה to an animal חטאת is the base for the argument between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about how the head is separated. That argument decides what הותזו means.
